title: Security assessment: protocol-ctf lab servers
boundary: The nine lab servers under protocol-ctf/challenges/ (WebSocket, gRPC and AI-agent tracks), each bound to 127.0.0.1. Remediation was assessed against the reference fixes in protocol-ctf/solutions/.

tester.name: security-research maintainers
tester.independence: Not independent: the testers also wrote the lab servers. This is a dogfood engagement to exercise the report tooling. A client engagement would use a tester independent of the code's authors.

methodology: Static analysis with our ESLint security plugins at their strict configs. Then manual exploitation of each server with the reference exploit, a negative control to confirm the exploit is what gets the flag, and a retest of the reference fix: the functional check must pass and the exploit must be blocked.
limitations: The labs are intentionally vulnerable. Findings are real for this code but were placed on purpose. AI-track servers use a deterministic toy model, not a production LLM.
outOfScope: The CTF CLI (ctf.mjs), shared libraries under lib/, dependencies, and deployment. The labs run only on loopback.
summary: Nine intentionally placed vulnerabilities were confirmed by exploitation, and one further weakness was found by static analysis. Every placed vulnerability has a reference fix that passes its functional check and blocks the exploit on retest. The non-constant-time password comparison in ws-1 is unfixed in both the vulnerable and the fixed server. Static analysis with our own plugins found the root cause of 3 of the 7 vulnerabilities a code scanner could be expected to find.
